title: Transduction Mechanism Matcher
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Join each physical property to the material mechanism that senses it and the electrical output it produces, with hints that name the missing idea rather than the answer.

learningObjectives: Attribute each of the station's sensors to the physical mechanism it uses.
Explain the chain from physical property through material change to electrical output.
prerequisites: Chapter 4 sections on what transduction means

keyQuestions: What does the middle column actually do, in every case?
Which two chains end in the same electrical output, and why is that not a problem?
The BME280 measures three things. How many different mechanisms is that?
commonMisconceptions: Treating a sensor as a single indivisible component.
Assuming every sensor ultimately produces a voltage.
Confusing the mechanism named "capacitance change" with the output named the same thing - one is what happens in the material, the other is what the circuit sees.
assessmentOpportunities: Attributes each sensor to its physical mechanism without prompting.
Describes a sensor as a three-link chain rather than a black box.
Explains why two sensors can share an output type and still measure different things.
